headline: Critical Java4Shell flaw enables remote code execution in Java apps
summary: A critical OpenJDK vulnerability called Java4Shell, disclosed by Oracle, lets unauthenticated attackers remotely execute code or crash the JVM on major Java applications including Jenkins, Atlassian Jira, Confluence, and Keycloak.

claims.statement: A critical OpenJDK vulnerability called Java4Shell allows unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute code on major Java applications.

sources.quote: Critical Java4Shell flaw allows RCE attacks on major Java applications
Attackers can crash the JVM or achieve unauthenticated RCE

claims.statement: Affected applications include Jenkins, Atlassian Jira, Confluence, and Keycloak.

sources.quote: including Jenkins, Atlassian Jira, Confluence, and Keycloak.

claims.statement: Attackers can also crash the JVM, not only achieve RCE.

sources.quote: Attackers can crash the JVM or achieve unauthenticated RCE
Oracle reveals fix-this-ASAP-grade Java4Shell bug that allows attacks on many third-party apps
